lines.en: Hi Omar! Why were you arguing with the TV last night?
Hi Sara. The election debate was on. It is easier to win an election with a slogan than to govern with one.
What a society argues about in public tells you what it values in private.
The proposal they fought over was popular, persuasive, and, on closer inspection, completely unaffordable.
Not until citizens can criticize power without fear is freedom of speech more than a decoration.
Enough politics. At least my job is calm. We only have six meetings a day.
Six! Were every meeting to end with a decision and a name, half the meetings would disappear.
What distinguishes a professional email from a casual one is not length, but the clarity of what happens next. Our emails clarify nothing.
It is advised that all feedback be specific, actionable, and kind; two out of three is not enough.
My manager's feedback is usually one out of three, and it is not the kind part.
Then let us laugh about it. That is cheaper than quitting.
What makes a pun work is not the joke itself, but the split second it takes the listener to catch it.
It is said that a pun is the lowest form of wit, usually by people who cannot make one.
However old a joke may be, it is new to anyone hearing it for the first time. Like my grandfather's jokes, which are new to every guest.
Speaking of your grandfather, does he still tell the story about the train?
Every Friday. What we remember is rarely what happened; it is the story we have told ourselves about what happened.
My brother tells the same story completely differently. Rarely do two siblings remember the same childhood.
It is unsettling to realize that every time we recall a memory, we rewrite it a little.
Then maybe the future will fix our memories.
What makes the future so hard to predict is not that it is hidden, but that it has not decided yet.
It is said that the best way to predict the future is to invent it.
Were anyone in the year 1900 to describe today's world, it would have sounded like madness, not foresight.
However precise the forecast, the future retains the right to surprise us.
Not until a technology disappears into daily life do we stop calling it new.
So what do you predict for yourself, Omar?
Little is certain about the coming years, except that they will not resemble my plans for them.
That is the wisest prediction I have heard.
Rarely has the future arrived on schedule; it tends to come early, late, or dressed as something else.
Then let us at least be early for lunch. My treat.
Now that is a forecast I can support. See you at the restaurant.
